texts.facts: (SC No.262/22) Indian Arms Act, 1959 & Arms Rules, 1962 04 52/2013 of Section - 120B IPC & Sections - 25 Amrabad PS (1)(b) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 05 145/2016 of Sections - 384,385, 386, 395 & 120B Bail applications Achampet PS IPC & Sections - 25 (1)(a) & 27 (1) were dismissed (PRC 31/2022) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 06 29/2005 of Utkoor Sections - 302 & 201 of IPC PS 07 393/2011 of Sultan Sections - 302, 342, 120B & 201 r/w Bazar PS 149 of IPC (SC 672/2017) 08 473/2011 of Sections - 302, 201 & 365 r/w 120B Pahadishareef PS IPC (PRC 19/2013) 09 177/2014 of Sections - 147, 148, 332, 115, 157, Nalgonda II-Town 158, 302, 120B, 201 & 202 r/w 149 PS IPC & Sections - 25 (1)(a), 25 (1)(b), 25 (1B) (g) & 27 of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 5. As per the contents of the order of detention and the counter filed by respondent No.2, the allegations levelled against the detenu in the aforesaid crimes/cases are that he was Member of banned Peoples War Naxalite Group (PWG). Thereafter, he closely associated with notorious Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/ 2 Gangster, namely Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem. KL,J & PSS,J 6. Perusal of the record would reveal that the detenu and his wife i.e., the writ petitioner herein were arrested in TADA Case by the Police of Sanathnagar Police Station in the year 1993. The Police have seized his Auto-rickshaw, Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Only) cash given by Shakamuri Appa Rao, an active Member of the banned PWG, who involved in K.S. Vyas, IPS (former DIG of Police) Murder Case. The Police have also seized grenade empty cups. Prisoner on Transit (PT) warrants were issued against the detenu and his wife. The same were executed and he was sent to Musheerabad Jail, where he came into contact with notorious Gangster, Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and his associate, who was also in Jail in K.S. Vyas, IPS murder case. According to the respondent authorities, the detenu continued his connections with Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and involved in nine (09) murder cases and extortion cases. After the death of Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem in the year 2016, he went into anonymity for some period. Thereafter, he started dealing with Real Estate Brokers to create his own image in the Society. In the said process, he developed friendship with Mohd. Abdullah @ Suresh Goud and other realtors for settlement of disputes by showing the weapons (firearms). He possessed one country made pistol KL,J & PSS,J chambering 7.65 mm caliber semi rimmed metallic cartridges which was fired previously. It is in working condition. The aforesaid cartridge is company made and is live. The detenu with his illegal acts created terror, panic and fear in the minds of the general public by using prohibited firearm and thereby committed the aforesaid offences and disturbed public order and also tranquility in the area. Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which would disturb the public order, respondent No.2 issued the impugned detention order dated 25.12.2022. The same was approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2457, dated 31.12.2022 and confirmed vide G.O.Rt.No.321, dated 28.02.2023. 7. Mr. Basa Chanakya, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the aforesaid eleven (11) crimes were referred, the same were not relied on by respondent No.2, the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order. The aforesaid two (02) crimes have to be read in isolation. Therefore, the aforesaid 11 cases are stale cases and the same cannot be considered for the purpose of issuance of detention order. In the aforesaid two (02) crimes relied upon by respondent No.2, the detaining authority while issuing detention order, he has not considered the fact that the allegation KL,J & PSS,J against the detenu is that he has possessed firearms illegally, but he has not used the said firearms in any crime. i) He would further submit that the detenu has not committed any incident/act, such as murder etc. Even then, respondent No.2 invoked his powers under Act No.1 of 1986 and issued the impugned detention order. The detenu did not attempt by using the alleged firearms and he has not brandished any offence. Even as per the counter and the impugned detention order, the detenu did not commit any offence after 2016. Even then, respondent No.2 issued impugned detention order illegally. There was no material before respondent No.2 to come to subjective satisfaction with regard to the disturbance caused to the public order due to the alleged acts committed by the detenu. With the aforesaid submissions, learned counsel sought to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned detention order and the consequential approval and confirmation orders. As discussed above, though the aforesaid eleven (11) crimes/cases were referred, respondent No.2, the detaining authority, relied upon the aforesaid two (02) crimes only and issued the impugned detention order. The detenu filed bail applications in the aforesaid crimes and the same were dismissed. 10. In Crime No.69 of 2005 pending on the file of Balmoor Police Station, the bail applications filed by the detenu were dismissed. The offences alleged against him are punishable under Sections - 363 & 302 r/w 34 IPC & Sections - 25 (1)(a) & 27 (1) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959. . (1988) 2 SCC 57 . (1988) 1 SCC 296 KL,J & PSS,J 11. In Crime No.124 of 2013 pending on the file of Achampet Police Station, the offences alleged against the detenu are punishable under Sections - 148, 120B, & 302 r/w 149 IPC & Sections - 25 (1)(a) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 & Arms Rules, 1962. The bail applications filed by the detenu were dismissed. 12. In Crime No.145 of 2016 pending on the file of Achampet Police Station, the offences alleged against the detenu are punishable under Sections - 384,385, 386, 395 & 120B IPC & Sections - 25 Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/ 4 (1)(a) & 27 (1) of the Indian Arms Act, 1959. Even in other crimes, PT warrants were issued against the detenu and the police have executed the same. Thus, the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature. He and his wife, the writ petitioner herein, were Members of PWG. PT warrants were executed against them.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana1 and Smt. T. Usha Bhai v. The State of Telangana2. . 2022 SCC OnLine SC 424 . 2022 LiveLaw (Tel) 94 (W.P. No.34934 of 2022, decided on 09.11.2022) KL,J & PSS,J iii) 8. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature and he possessed the aforesaid firearms illegally. The aforesaid firearms which are prohibited were seized from the detenu. The detenu was the Member of banned PWG and closely associated with notorious Gangster Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and his associates. After his death, the detenu was moving closely with Realtors and settled several real-estate disputes by threatening innocents by showing firearms. Thus, according to him, the petitioner is a notorious and dangerous criminal. He is an 'Arms Offender'. Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences, the impugned detention order was issued by respondent No.2 and the same was approved and confirmed by respondent No.1. There is no error in it. i) Learned Special Government Pleader has placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay KL,J & PSS,J Kumar v. Union of India3 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh4. 9. 14. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration5 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. . . In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar6, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are. (1966) 1 SCR 709 KL,J & PSS,J under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances. It will thus appear Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/ 5 that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". One has to imagine three concentric circles. Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State. It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State." 16. In Mallada K. Sri Ram1, the Apex Court considering the fact that only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu and he was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, [LEAKAGE_MASK] the detention order. 17. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar7, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean . AIR 1984 SC 1334 KL,J & PSS,J 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'. The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general. 21. In Smt. K. Aruna Kumari4, the Apex Court held that this Court cannot examine probative value of evidence available to the detaining authority. Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/ 6 22. 23. In Smt. T. Usha Bhai2, the detaining authority invoked the preventive detention order against the husband of the petitioner, a sitting MLA on the allegation of giving hate speeches.
